chunks.heading: What is the purpose of Form PENS.A/2, and what happens if I don't complete it?
chunks.text: All participants in the Fund are encouraged to complete form PENS.A/2 to specify the recipient(s) of any residual settlement that may become due under Article 38 of the UNJSPF Regulations, Rules and Pension Adjustment System and Section B.5 of the UNJSPF Administrative Rules, as well as any retroactive due but unpaid benefit owing at the time of their death under Section J.3 of the UNJSPF Administrative Rules. If there is no duly completed, dated and signed PENS.A/2 in the Fund's records, any residual settlement and/or retroactive due but unpaid benefit will be paid to your estate instead.

chunks.heading: When does a residual settlement become payable?
chunks.text: A residual settlement becomes payable if: (a) the participant died in service with no survivors (spouse, former spouse, child under 21, disabled child, or secondary dependant) entitled to a benefit under Articles 34, 35 bis, 35 ter, 36 or 37; (b) the participant died after service but before electing a benefit, with five or more years of contributory service and no such entitled survivors; (c) the participant died during entitlement to a retirement, early retirement, deferred retirement or disability benefit, with no further benefits payable to survivors and the total benefits already paid were less than the participant's own contributions plus interest; or (d) the participant had entitled survivors and, following the death of the participant and the death or termination of entitlement of all survivors, the total amount paid by the Fund is less than the participant's own contributions plus interest.

chunks.heading: When does a retroactive due but unpaid benefit arise?
chunks.text: A retroactive due but unpaid benefit arises if, at the time of the participant's death, a benefit was payable but had not yet been disbursed — including retirement, early retirement, deferred retirement, and disability benefits, or a withdrawal settlement that was due but not paid at death, including payments that may have been returned by the participant's bank but were properly payable.

chunks.heading: Who can be designated as a recipient on Form PENS.A/2?
chunks.text: You may designate any individual or institution as recipient(s). If you designate an institution, you must confirm with that entity that it is able to receive donations as a designated recipient. If the Fund is unable to make the payment to a designated institution, or the institution refuses to accept the payment, the amount will be distributed among any other surviving designated recipients in the ratio of their own shares when payment is due, or, failing such surviving recipients, to your estate.

chunks.heading: How many recipients can be designated, and how is the settlement shared?
chunks.text: You can designate as many recipients as you wish. If more than one recipient is designated, they will share the residual settlement and/or retroactive due but unpaid benefit equally, unless otherwise indicated. The share of a designated recipient who predeceases you will be distributed among any surviving designated recipients in the ratio of their own shares.

chunks.heading: How do I find or request my Unique Identification Number (UID) for Section 1 of Form PENS.A/2?
chunks.text: If you do not know your Unique Identification number, send an email to requestUIDonly@unjspf.org. If you are a current participant, you must request your UID by sending an email from your work email address (which serves as identity verification), including your index number and/or six-digit Pension Fund number. If you separated and no longer have access to your work email address, include your full name, last employing organization before separation, last duty station, and five-digit alphanumeric retirement number so the Member Self-Service (MSS) support team can verify your identity.

chunks.heading: What are the pension number and retirement number fields in Section 1, and are they required?
chunks.text: The pension number field is required — it can be found on your pension statement or in the welcome letter from UNJSPF, and your new designation will apply to the pension number (participation account) you specify. The retirement number field is optional and can be found in your benefit letter from UNJSPF.

chunks.heading: How should I provide recipient information in Section 2, and what are the share requirements?
chunks.text: Provide the recipient's full name exactly as shown on their passport or official government-issued photo ID, along with date of birth, sex, contact information, and relationship to you. Clearly indicate each recipient's share — multiple shares must total 100 per cent; if shares are not indicated or do not total 100 per cent, multiple recipients will share equally.

chunks.heading: What additional information is needed if a designated recipient is a minor or an institution?
chunks.text: If designating a minor, provide the contact information of the parent or appointed legal guardian who has custody of the minor in the additional information field. If the recipient is an institution, provide the institution's full name, contact information, and registration or identification number, plus the full name and contact information of a contact person, on a separate page.

chunks.heading: What do I do if I want to designate more than four recipients?
chunks.text: Check the appropriate box at the end of Section 2 and attach additional duly dated and hand-signed sheet(s); the date on the additional sheet(s) must match the date on Form PENS.A/2.

chunks.heading: What makes Form PENS.A/2 valid, and how do I change my designation later?
chunks.text: The form must be completed in full, dated, and signed to be valid. You may alter your designation of a recipient at any time by submitting a new form, which supersedes all previous designations. It is your responsibility to keep your designation up to date to reflect your current situation — for example, after a change in marital or family status. A new form must be completed for each new participation in the Fund. It's suggested you keep a copy of the completed form with your other important documents. For further guidance, contact the secretary of your Staff Pension Committee, or UNJSPF directly if you are a retiree or staff member of the United Nations family (e.g. UN Secretariat, UNDP, UNFPA, UNHCR, UNICEF).

chunks.heading: When and how does Section 4 (Signature Authentication) need to be completed?
chunks.text: Section 4 is only applicable if one of the designated recipients is an institution. For UNJSPF to accept your signature as duly authenticated, you must sign and date the form in the presence of an authenticating official (e.g. a United Nations official, government official, or notary public). That official must complete all fields in Section 4: printed full name, email address, official title/licence or index number, original ink signature, authentication date (which must match the date you signed the form), and official stamp/seal of office.

chunks.heading: How do I submit Form PENS.A/2 electronically through Member Self-Service (MSS)?
chunks.text: Most registered MSS users can submit UNJSPF forms electronically under the "MSS Document Upload" tab. Download the relevant form under the "E-Forms" tab, complete it, print it, date and hand-sign it, then scan it and upload it (in JPG, JPEG, or PDF format) via MSS. Once successfully submitted electronically, there is no need to also submit a physical copy. Note that access to the "MSS Document Upload" tab may be restricted at the request of some UNJSPF member organizations, in which case that tab won't appear as an MSS menu option — participants should first check with their employing organization on the correct submission process.

chunks.heading: How do I submit Form PENS.A/2 by mail if I'm not using MSS?
chunks.text: You can mail the physical, duly completed, dated and hand-signed form directly to UNJSPF. By regular postal mail to the New York office: United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund, c/o United Nations, PO Box 5036, New York, NY 10163-5036, United States of America. By express courier (e.g. DHL) or registered mail to the New York office: United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund, 37th floor 1 DHP, 885 Second Avenue, New York, NY 10017, United States of America. To the Geneva office (by postal mail or express courier): United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund, c/o Palais des Nations, 1211 Genève 10, Suisse.
